name: R1

source.quote: Unitree designs R1 humanoid robot to be agile and affordable
The 25-kilogram robot combines dynamic movement capabilities with a built-in Large Multimodal AI Model
features 26 degrees of freedom across its legs, waist, arms, and head

review.reason: The reviewed source did not establish both the exact recorded value and the concrete robot variant for this specification.

source.quote: Unitree R1 humanoid robot is capable of walking, running, cartwheeling, doing kung-fu, falling on its own will, and getting up like nothing ever happened.

locomotion.note: Two-legged humanoid; walking/running/cartwheeling behavior and the 'run'/'fall-recovery' capability entries above are two-legged gait, not wheeled.

source.quote: The standard model was priced at $5,900

timeline.detail: Unveiled with a $5,900 starting price, undercutting Unitree's own G1 ($16k) and H1 ($90k).

source.quote: The low price targets universities, hobbyists and early consumer adopters who were priced out of Unitree's $16 k G1 and $90 k H1

timeline.detail: R1 is listed for direct purchase on Unitree's own store at $4,900, with buyers directed to contact Unitree for further product information.

source.quote: If you want to know more product information, please contact us directly
Unitree R1 humanoid robot is capable of walking, running, cartwheeling, doing kung-fu, falling on its own will, and getting up like nothing ever happened.

review.reason: The text source was reviewed, but no video segment was watched; the existing capability status and autonomy classification for the exact recorded robot variant were not fully verified.

capabilities.note: This launch-video coverage does not itself state who controlled the robot. Autonomy is set to 'teleoperated' on the strength of The Robot Report's separate, explicit statement that 'Unitree's R1 is remote-controlled' and that 'Autonomy is achievable but requires secondary development' (https://www.therobotreport.com/unitree-designs-r1-humanoid-robot-to-be-agile-and-affordable/, accessed 2026-09-20) -- a general characterization of the shipped R1 platform, not a clip-specific statement about this particular run.

source.quote: falling on its own will, and getting up like nothing ever happened

review.reason: The text source was reviewed, but no video segment was watched; the existing capability status and autonomy classification for the exact recorded robot variant were not fully verified.

capabilities.note: Same launch-video coverage as the 'run' entry above; autonomy is likewise inferred from The Robot Report's general 'remote-controlled' statement about the R1 platform rather than a clip-specific control statement.

sdk.note: unitree_sdk2 ships a dedicated r1/ example folder (github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2/tree/main/example, accessed 2026-09-21) alongside g1, h1, h2, confirming R1 support in the same generic Unitree SDK; unitree_ros2 layers ROS2 on top via CycloneDDS.

notes: Height/price conflict: The Robot Report's July 2025 launch coverage gives 1.2 m (3.9 ft) and a $5,900 standard price, while Unitree's own current store page (accessed 2026-09-20) states '123 cm' and lists the base unit at $4,900. Both are recorded here; the discrepancy is not resolved.

The Robot Report notes the R1 'is remote-controlled rather than autonomous. Autonomy is achievable but requires secondary development' — relevant context for any 'demonstrated' autonomy claims made elsewhere about this robot.

Battery runtime, walking speed and payload were not found on a primary source during this build and are omitted rather than guessed; secondary aggregators (RoboZaps, Humanoid.guide) cite ~1 hour runtime but this was not independently confirmed against a manufacturer or press primary source.
No named-customer delivery evidence was found; delivery.status stays 'claimed'.
